public_rationale: The claim has two parts. First, you cannot count on Imagen to interpret every prompt correctly. Second, this is because its language understanding is weak. Benchmark work from mid-2025 (OneIG-Bench) ranks Imagen 4 among the best at following prompts. It also says many models confuse which attribute belongs to which subject. But the readable text gives no failure rate for Imagen 4. On the cause, an August 2025 test found a Google image model that stated the correct clock time in text and then drew it wrong. That points to rendering or training-data bias rather than language understanding, but it involves a different model. The evidence fits the reliability part but does not settle the cause, so the claim stays unresolved.

our_interpretation: 'The system' means Imagen 4, and more broadly the leading text-to-image models of mid-2025.

There are two parts. (1) Reliability: the models often get unusual prompts wrong, such as reversed roles, matching attributes to the right objects, or clock times. (2) Cause: these failures come from weak understanding of the prompt's language, not only from other limits such as rendering or training-data bias.
The period is mid-2025, when the post was written.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled tests or benchmarks of Imagen 4 (or its peers) from about mid-2025 show frequent failures on unusual prompts, and the evidence links those failures to misreading the prompt rather than to other causes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Controlled tests show that Imagen 4 reliably follows unusual compositional prompts, or that its failures come from something other than language understanding (for example, it reads the prompt correctly but cannot draw it).
